paragraphs.text: translated by
1. THIS, singer, is my firm determination, to aid the worshipper who pours the Soma.
paragraphs.original: असत्सु मे जरितः साभिवेगो यत्सुन्वते यजमानाय शिक्षम् ।
paragraphs.translit: asatsu me jaritaḥ sābhivego yatsunvate yajamānāya śikṣam |

paragraphs.text: I slay the man who brings no milk oblation, unrighteous, powerful, the truth's perverter.
paragraphs.original: अनाशीर्दामहमस्मि प्रहन्ता सत्यध्वृतं वृजिनायन्तमाभुम्
paragraphs.translit: anāśīrdāmahamasmi prahantā satyadhvṛtaṃ vṛjināyantamābhum

paragraphs.text: 2. Then Will I, when I lead my friends to battle against the radiant persons of the godless,
paragraphs.original: यदीदहं युधये संनयान्यदेवयून्तन्वा शूशुजानान् ।
paragraphs.translit: yadīdahaṃ yudhaye saṃnayānyadevayūntanvā śūśujānān |

paragraphs.text: Prepare for thee at home a vigorous bullock, and pour for thee the fifteen-fold strong juices.
paragraphs.original: अमा ते तुम्रं वृषभं पचानि तीव्रं सुतं पञ्चदशं नि षिञ्चम्
paragraphs.translit: amā te tumraṃ vṛṣabhaṃ pacāni tīvraṃ sutaṃ pañcadaśaṃ ni ṣiñcam

paragraphs.text: 3. I know not him who sayeth and declareth that he hath slain the godless in the battle.
paragraphs.original: नाहं तं वेद य इति ब्रवीत्यदेवयून्समरणे जघन्वान् ।
paragraphs.translit: nāhaṃ taṃ veda ya iti bravītyadevayūnsamaraṇe jaghanvān |

paragraphs.text: Soon as they see the furious combat raging, men speak forth praises of my vigorous horses.
paragraphs.original: यदावाख्यत्समरणमृघावदादिद्ध मे वृषभा प्र ब्रुवन्ति
paragraphs.translit: yadāvākhyatsamaraṇamṛghāvadādiddha me vṛṣabhā pra bruvanti

paragraphs.text: 4. While yet my deeds of might were unrecorded, all passed for Maghavans though I existed.
paragraphs.original: यदज्ञातेषु वृजनेष्वासं विश्वे सतो मघवानो म आसन् ।
paragraphs.translit: yadajñāteṣu vṛjaneṣvāsaṃ viśve sato maghavāno ma āsan |

paragraphs.text: The potent one who dwelt in peace I conquered, grasped by the foot and slew him on the mountain.
paragraphs.original: जिनामि वेत्क्षेम आ सन्तमाभुं प्र तं क्षिणां पर्वते पादगृह्य
paragraphs.translit: jināmi vetkṣema ā santamābhuṃ pra taṃ kṣiṇāṃ parvate pādagṛhya

paragraphs.text: 5. None hinder me in mine heroic exploits, no, not the mountains when I will and purpose.
paragraphs.original: न वा उ मां वृजने वारयन्ते न पर्वतासो यदहं मनस्ये ।
paragraphs.translit: na vā u māṃ vṛjane vārayante na parvatāso yadahaṃ manasye |

paragraphs.text: Even the deaf will tremble at my roaring, and every day will dust be agitated.
paragraphs.original: मम स्वनात्कृधुकर्णो भयात एवेदनु द्यून्किरणः समेजात्
paragraphs.translit: mama svanātkṛdhukarṇo bhayāta evedanu dyūnkiraṇaḥ samejāt

paragraphs.text: 6. To see the Indraless oblation-drinkers, mean offerers, o'ertaken by destruction!
paragraphs.original: दर्शन्न्वत्र शृतपाँ अनिन्द्रान्बाहुक्षदः शरवे पत्यमानान् ।
paragraphs.translit: darśannvatra śṛtapām̐ anindrānbāhukṣadaḥ śarave patyamānān |

paragraphs.text: Then shall the fellies of my car pass over those who have blamed my joyous Friend and scorned him.
paragraphs.original: घृषुं वा ये निनिदुः सखायमध्यू न्वेषु पवयो ववृत्युः
paragraphs.translit: ghṛṣuṃ vā ye niniduḥ sakhāyamadhyū nveṣu pavayo vavṛtyuḥ

paragraphs.text: 7. Thou wast, thou grewest to full vital vigour: an earlier saw, a later one shall see thee.
paragraphs.original: अभूर्वौक्षीर्व्यु आयुरानड्दर्षन्नु पूर्वो अपरो नु दर्षत् ।
paragraphs.translit: abhūrvaukṣīrvyu āyurānaḍdarṣannu pūrvo aparo nu darṣat |

paragraphs.text: Two canopies, as 'twere, are round about him who reacheth to the limit of this region.
paragraphs.original: द्वे पवस्ते परि तं न भूतो यो अस्य पारे रजसो विवेष
paragraphs.translit: dve pavaste pari taṃ na bhūto yo asya pāre rajaso viveṣa

paragraphs.text: 8. The freed kine eat the barley of the pious. 1 saw them as they wandered with the herdsman.
paragraphs.original: गावो यवं प्रयुता अर्यो अक्षन्ता अपश्यं सहगोपाश्चरन्तीः ।
paragraphs.translit: gāvo yavaṃ prayutā aryo akṣantā apaśyaṃ sahagopāścarantīḥ |

paragraphs.text: The calling of the pious rang around them. What portion will these kine afford their owner?
paragraphs.original: हवा इदर्यो अभितः समायन्कियदासु स्वपतिश्छन्दयाते
paragraphs.translit: havā idaryo abhitaḥ samāyankiyadāsu svapatiśchandayāte

paragraphs.text: 9. When we who cat the grass of men are gathered I am with barley-eaters in the corn-land.
paragraphs.original: सं यद्वयं यवसादो जनानामहं यवाद उर्वज्रे अन्तः ।
paragraphs.translit: saṃ yadvayaṃ yavasādo janānāmahaṃ yavāda urvajre antaḥ |

paragraphs.text: There shall the captor yoke the yokeless bullock, and he who hath been yoked seek one to loose him.
paragraphs.original: अत्रा युक्तोऽवसातारमिच्छादथो अयुक्तं युनजद्ववन्वान्
paragraphs.translit: atrā yukto'vasātāramicchādatho ayuktaṃ yunajadvavanvān

paragraphs.text: 10. There wilt thou hold as true my spoken purpose, to bring together quadrupeds. and bipeds.
paragraphs.original: अत्रेदु मे मंससे सत्यमुक्तं द्विपाच्च यच्चतुष्पात्संसृजानि ।
paragraphs.translit: atredu me maṃsase satyamuktaṃ dvipācca yaccatuṣpātsaṃsṛjāni |

paragraphs.text: I will divide, without a fight, his riches who warreth here, against the Bull, with women.
paragraphs.original: स्त्रीभिर्यो अत्र वृषणं पृतन्यादयुद्धो अस्य वि भजानि वेदः
paragraphs.translit: strībhiryo atra vṛṣaṇaṃ pṛtanyādayuddho asya vi bhajāni vedaḥ

paragraphs.text: 11. When a man's daughter hath been ever eyeless, who, knowing, will be wroth with her for blindness?
paragraphs.original: यस्यानक्षा दुहिता जात्वास कस्तां विद्वाँ अभि मन्याते अन्धाम् ।
paragraphs.translit: yasyānakṣā duhitā jātvāsa kastāṃ vidvām̐ abhi manyāte andhām |

paragraphs.text: Which of the two will loose on him his anger-the man who leads her home or he who woos her?
paragraphs.original: कतरो मेनिं प्रति तं मुचाते य ईं वहाते य ईं वा वरेयात्
paragraphs.translit: kataro meniṃ prati taṃ mucāte ya īṃ vahāte ya īṃ vā vareyāt

paragraphs.text: 12. How many a maid is pleasing to the suitor who fain would marry for her splendid riches?
paragraphs.original: कियती योषा मर्यतो वधूयोः परिप्रीता पन्यसा वार्येण ।
paragraphs.translit: kiyatī yoṣā maryato vadhūyoḥ pariprītā panyasā vāryeṇa |

paragraphs.text: If the girl be both good and fair of feature, she finds, herself, a friend among the people.
paragraphs.original: भद्रा वधूर्भवति यत्सुपेशाः स्वयं सा मित्रं वनुते जने चित्
paragraphs.translit: bhadrā vadhūrbhavati yatsupeśāḥ svayaṃ sā mitraṃ vanute jane cit

paragraphs.text: 13. His feet have grasped: he eats the man who meets him. Around his head he sets the head for shelter.
paragraphs.original: पत्तो जगार प्रत्यञ्चमत्ति शीर्ष्णा शिरः प्रति दधौ वरूथम् ।
paragraphs.translit: patto jagāra pratyañcamatti śīrṣṇā śiraḥ prati dadhau varūtham |

paragraphs.text: Sitting anear and right above he smites us, and follows earth that lies spread out beneath him.
paragraphs.original: आसीन ऊर्ध्वामुपसि क्षिणाति न्यङ्ङुत्तानामन्वेति भूमिम्
paragraphs.translit: āsīna ūrdhvāmupasi kṣiṇāti nyaṅṅuttānāmanveti bhūmim

paragraphs.text: 14. High, leafless, shadowless, and swift is Heaven: the Mother stands, the Youngling, loosed, is feeding.
paragraphs.original: बृहन्नच्छायो अपलाशो अर्वा तस्थौ माता विषितो अत्ति गर्भः ।
paragraphs.translit: bṛhannacchāyo apalāśo arvā tasthau mātā viṣito atti garbhaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Loud hath she lowed, licking Another's offspring. In what world hath the Cow laid down her udder?
paragraphs.original: अन्यस्या वत्सं रिहती मिमाय कया भुवा नि दधे धेनुरूधः
paragraphs.translit: anyasyā vatsaṃ rihatī mimāya kayā bhuvā ni dadhe dhenurūdhaḥ

paragraphs.text: 15. Seven heroes from the nether part ascended, and from the upper part came eight together.
paragraphs.original: सप्त वीरासो अधरादुदायन्नष्टोत्तरात्तात्समजग्मिरन्ते ।
paragraphs.translit: sapta vīrāso adharādudāyannaṣṭottarāttātsamajagmirante |

paragraphs.text: Nine from behind came armed with winnowing-baskets: ten from the front pressed o'er the rock's high ridges.
paragraphs.original: नव पश्चातात्स्थिविमन्त आयन्दश प्राक्सानु वि तिरन्त्यश्नः
paragraphs.translit: nava paścātātsthivimanta āyandaśa prāksānu vi tirantyaśnaḥ

paragraphs.text: 16. One of the ten, the tawny, shared in common, they send to execute their final purpose.
paragraphs.original: दशानामेकं कपिलं समानं तं हिन्वन्ति क्रतवे पार्याय ।
paragraphs.translit: daśānāmekaṃ kapilaṃ samānaṃ taṃ hinvanti kratave pāryāya |

paragraphs.text: The Mother carries on her breast the Infant of noble form and soothes it while it knows not.
paragraphs.original: गर्भं माता सुधितं वक्षणास्ववेनन्तं तुषयन्ती बिभर्ति
paragraphs.translit: garbhaṃ mātā sudhitaṃ vakṣaṇāsvavenantaṃ tuṣayantī bibharti

paragraphs.text: 17. The Heroes dressed with fire the fatted weather: the dice were thrown by way of sport and gaming.
paragraphs.original: पीवानं मेषमपचन्त वीरा न्युप्ता अक्षा अनु दीव आसन् ।
paragraphs.translit: pīvānaṃ meṣamapacanta vīrā nyuptā akṣā anu dīva āsan |

paragraphs.text: Two reach the plain amid the heavenly waters, hallowing and with means of purifying.
paragraphs.original: द्वा धनुं बृहतीमप्स्वन्तः पवित्रवन्ता चरतः पुनन्ता
paragraphs.translit: dvā dhanuṃ bṛhatīmapsvantaḥ pavitravantā carataḥ punantā

paragraphs.text: 18. Crying aloud they ran in all directions: One half of them will cook, and not the other.
paragraphs.original: वि क्रोशनासो विष्वञ्च आयन्पचाति नेमो नहि पक्षदर्धः ।
paragraphs.translit: vi krośanāso viṣvañca āyanpacāti nemo nahi pakṣadardhaḥ |

paragraphs.text: To me hath Savitar, this God, declared it: He will perform, whose food is wood and butter.
paragraphs.original: अयं मे देवः सविता तदाह द्र्वन्न इद्वनवत्सर्पिरन्नः
paragraphs.translit: ayaṃ me devaḥ savitā tadāha drvanna idvanavatsarpirannaḥ

paragraphs.text: 19. I saw a troop advancing from the distance moved, not by wheels but their own God-like nature.
paragraphs.original: अपश्यं ग्रामं वहमानमारादचक्रया स्वधया वर्तमानम् ।
paragraphs.translit: apaśyaṃ grāmaṃ vahamānamārādacakrayā svadhayā vartamānam |

paragraphs.text: The Friendly One seeks human generations, destroying, still new bands of evil beings.
paragraphs.original: सिषक्त्यर्यः प्र युगा जनानां सद्यः शिश्ना प्रमिनानो नवीयान्
paragraphs.translit: siṣaktyaryaḥ pra yugā janānāṃ sadyaḥ śiśnā pramināno navīyān

paragraphs.text: 20. These my two Bulls, even Pramara's, are harnessed: drive them not far; here let them often linger.
paragraphs.original: एतौ मे गावौ प्रमरस्य युक्तौ मो षु प्र सेधीर्मुहुरिन्ममन्धि ।
paragraphs.translit: etau me gāvau pramarasya yuktau mo ṣu pra sedhīrmuhurinmamandhi |

paragraphs.text: The waters even shall aid him to his object, and the all-cleansing Sun who is above us.
paragraphs.original: आपश्चिदस्य वि नशन्त्यर्थं सूरश्च मर्क उपरो बभूवान्
paragraphs.translit: āpaścidasya vi naśantyarthaṃ sūraśca marka uparo babhūvān

paragraphs.text: 21. This is the thunderbolt which often whirleth down from the lofty misty realm of Surya.
paragraphs.original: अयं यो वज्रः पुरुधा विवृत्तोऽवः सूर्यस्य बृहतः पुरीषात् ।
paragraphs.translit: ayaṃ yo vajraḥ purudhā vivṛtto'vaḥ sūryasya bṛhataḥ purīṣāt |

paragraphs.text: Beyond this realm there is another glory so through old age they pass and feel no sorrow.
paragraphs.original: श्रव इदेना परो अन्यदस्ति तदव्यथी जरिमाणस्तरन्ति
paragraphs.translit: śrava idenā paro anyadasti tadavyathī jarimāṇastaranti

paragraphs.text: 22. Bound fast to,every tree the cow is lowing, and thence the man-consuming birds are flying,
paragraphs.original: वृक्षेवृक्षे नियता मीमयद्गौस्ततो वयः प्र पतान्पूरुषादः ।
paragraphs.translit: vṛkṣevṛkṣe niyatā mīmayadgaustato vayaḥ pra patānpūruṣādaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Then all this world, though pressing juice for Indra and strengthening the Rsi, is affrighted.
paragraphs.original: अथेदं विश्वं भुवनं भयात इन्द्राय सुन्वदृषये च शिक्षत्
paragraphs.translit: athedaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ bhayāta indrāya sunvadṛṣaye ca śikṣat

paragraphs.text: 23. In the Gods' mansion stood the first-created, and from their separation came the later.
paragraphs.original: देवानां माने प्रथमा अतिष्ठन्कृन्तत्रादेषामुपरा उदायन् ।
paragraphs.translit: devānāṃ māne prathamā atiṣṭhankṛntatrādeṣāmuparā udāyan |

paragraphs.text: Three warm the Earth while holding stores of water, and Two of these convey the murmuring moisture.
paragraphs.original: त्रयस्तपन्ति पृथिवीमनूपा द्वा बृबूकं वहतः पुरीषम्
paragraphs.translit: trayastapanti pṛthivīmanūpā dvā bṛbūkaṃ vahataḥ purīṣam

paragraphs.text: 24. This is thy life: and do thou mark and know it. As such, hide not thyself in time of battle.
paragraphs.original: सा ते जीवातुरुत तस्य विद्धि मा स्मैतादृगप गूहः समर्ये ।
paragraphs.translit: sā te jīvāturuta tasya viddhi mā smaitādṛgapa gūhaḥ samarye |

paragraphs.text: He manifests the light and hides the vapour: his foot is never free from robes that veil it.
paragraphs.original: आविः स्वः कृणुते गूहते बुसं स पादुरस्य निर्णिजो न मुच्यते
paragraphs.translit: āviḥ svaḥ kṛṇute gūhate busaṃ sa pādurasya nirṇijo na mucyate
